Hi Emma — great questions and thanks for the spreadsheet (got it). Quick recap below; attaching a compact worksheet that maps your session profile into tokens/month and cost scenarios.

Short answers up top:
- Estimated tokens/month per 1M MAU (your profile): ~420M–520M tokens depending on session frequency assumptions.
- Indicative unit economics (list vs committed): $12–$18 / 1M tokens (list). With a 12–18 month committed volume, committed pricing target we typically land in the $6–$9 / 1M tokens range depending on concurrency SLAs and batch/caching allowances.
- Continuous batching impact on p95: negligible for streaming short-turn flows if you allow 50–120ms scheduling headroom; our routable latency SLO can stay under 350–400ms p95 for 40–60 tokens output with an optimized concurrency window.

What I attached (neha-econ-worksheet.pdf):
- Assumptions tab: session frequency (avg sessions/user/day), token mix distribution (sum, q&a), and cacheable prefix %
- Token estimate: low/medium/high scenarios mapping to 1M MAU
- Pricing model: three lanes — Hosted list, Committed dedicated, Private deployment (estimates)
- Batching profile: recommended continuous batching window sizes by workload (interactive vs async), and expected CPU/GPU efficiency uplift (20–35%)

Next steps I suggest:
1) Ben to propose an initial committed band (monthly tokens) and a draft SLA that balances your p95 requirement and price target.
2) Lauren to flag any procurement/regulatory concerns (data residency if needed) for the pricing lanes.
3) Internal knob: decide whether you want a cache-first approach (higher cache %, lower tokens) vs. conversation-state full evaluation.

Ben / Lauren — can you two pick this up and I’ll join any follow-ups? Emma — happy to hop on a 30m call tomorrow or Thursday to go line-by-line if that helps.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha / Emma — following up with a proposed committed band and an initial econ sketch below. This is intended to be a starting point for procurement conversations.

Proposed monthly committed bands (tokens/month):
- Band A (conservative): 200M tokens — list: $2,400 / month; committed target: $1,200 / month ($6 / 1M tokens)
- Band B (mid): 500M tokens — list: $6,000 / month; committed target: $3,250 / month (~$6.5 / 1M)
- Band C (aggressive): 1B tokens — list: $12,000 / month; committed target: $6,500 / month (~$6.5 / 1M)

Notes on concurrency & continuous batching:
- We model continuous batching by grouping inflight requests per model shard with a 30–60ms scheduling window for low-latency services. That yields 20–30% token cost reduction vs strictly single-request runs for your workload mix.
- If Ava requires hard 250ms p95 for interactive flows, we recommend a mixed routing policy: prioritize interactive requests onto a low-latency lane (reduced batching window, slightly higher unit cost) and send bulk/async traffic to batched lanes.

Questions for Emma (quick):
- What percentage of your workload is async/background (e.g., nightly summarization) vs interactive?
- Any hard compliance constraints that would push you to Private deployment early?

If those look reasonable I can draft a simple commercial term sheet and an initial draft SLA for the Band B case.

—Ben
